jobDescription: Copperline Kitchens operates 110 casual-dining restaurants. The Project Manager for restaurant technology plans and runs rollouts of kitchen and front-of-house systems, manages vendors and installation partners against contract milestones, designs site trials, and delivers rollouts into live trading across many sites, including go-live sign-off with each general manager and a hypercare period. A recognised project-management certification is required. Restaurants are run by general managers who sign off each go-live, and the project manager works with the operations director, the IT team and franchise partners. A new kitchen ordering system and handheld ordering devices are planned for next year.
requirements: Plans multi-site technology projects with a maintained schedule and RAID log.
Manages vendors and installation partners against contract milestones.
Has delivered a technology rollout into live trading at multiple sites, including go-live sign-off and hypercare.
Designs and runs site trials before wider rollout.

evidence.text: Project Coordinator, Bramble & Barrow Pubs, April 2022 to July 2024. Built the schedule and RAID log for the kitchen display screen project and updated both after each weekly vendor call, sending the RAID log to the operations director each Friday.
Tracked the screen vendor and the installation partner against the contract milestones, chasing two late hardware deliveries and recording the recovery dates agreed.
Set up a ten-week trial of kitchen display screens in three pubs, with the screens used alongside paper tickets during quieter weekday services while weekend services stayed on paper only.
Gathered cooks' and managers' feedback from the trial pubs through a short weekly form and summarised it for the operations director, grouping comments by kitchen station.
Wrote the trial close report, setting out the screen-layout changes needed before any wider rollout, with costs for the hardware changes.

Work sample: the trial plan for the kitchen display screens, naming the three trial pubs, the ten-week schedule, the weekday-only usage rule, the success measures and the criteria the operations director would use to decide on a wider rollout, signed by the operations director.

Reference call note: the referee, a franchisee who worked with the candidate, reported hearing from head office that the screens were switched on in all 64 pubs after the trial and that 'the whole estate runs on them now'.
HR verification note: the candidate's PRINCE2 Practitioner certificate number was checked on the awarding body's public register and is listed as current.

propositions.text: The candidate built and maintained the schedule and RAID log for the kitchen display screen project.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the schedule and RAID log work directly.

propositions.text: The candidate set up a ten-week trial of kitchen display screens in three pubs, used alongside paper tickets during weekday services.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the trial and the trial plan sets out its sites, schedule and usage rule.

propositions.text: The candidate delivered the kitchen display screens into live trading in all 64 pubs, with go-live sign-off and hypercare.
propositions.rationale: The rollout statement is the referee repeating what head office said, and it does not describe anything the candidate did; the documented work is a three-pub trial run alongside paper tickets. The deployment rule does not allow a trial to be described as live operation, and a second-hand report is not a source that says the rollout happened.

gold.expectedGap: Only the three-pub trial is documented; a multi-site rollout into live trading with go-live sign-off and hypercare is not.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the schedule, the vendor tracking, the three-pub trial and the verified certificate; record the estate-wide rollout as second-hand information from the referee.
followUpTargets: Ask whether the kitchen display screens were rolled out beyond the three trial pubs while the candidate was there, and what the candidate did for any go-live sign-off and hypercare.
